FCX.thesis_one_line: World-class copper and gold miner whose biggest mine is still recovering from a 2025 accident; the share price already assumes full recovery and strong copper.
kill_criteria: FY2026 consolidated copper sales guidance (now "approximate 3.1 billion pounds of copper", acc. 0000831259-26-000033) cut below 3.0bn lb, or PTFI production-rate milestones (65% H2'26, 80% mid-'27) pushed out, in any quarterly release.
FCX-defined net debt (consolidated debt less consolidated cash, excluding PTFI downstream project debt; currently $2.07bn at 30 Jun 2026) above $4.0bn.
Realised copper price below $4.50/lb for two consecutive quarters (Q2'26: $6.17).
Full-year 2026 consolidated unit net cash cost guidance above $2.25/lb (now "$1.90 per pound of copper for the year 2026", acc. 0000831259-26-000033).
PTFI IUPK extension beyond 2041 not formally granted by 31 Dec 2027.
key_adverse_facts: 2026 copper sales guidance was cut in April 2026 from 3.4bn lb to 3.1bn lb (gold 0.8Moz to 650koz) on Grasberg ramp-up delay; Grasberg at ~65% of capacity in H2 2026 and near full only by end-2027.

Q2'26 revenue -7.3% and operating margin -360 bps YoY: consolidated copper sales 710m lb vs 1,016m lb; idle-facility and restoration costs of $284m in Q2 ($690m H1) are excluded from adjusted EPS and unit costs.

Consolidated net debt is $5.3bn; the $2.1bn 'FCX net debt' excludes $3.2bn of PTFI smelter/refinery project debt. Noncontrolling interests are $12.1bn at book; PTFI is 48.76% owned but consolidated, so EV-based multiples overstate FCX's share.
Reverse DCF: price needs ~31% annual owner-FCF growth from a normalised $2.5bn (fading to 3%); base case is worth ~$50/share and bull ~$73 at a 10.4% cost of equity.
Indonesia: operating rights expire 2041; the Feb 2026 MOU cuts FCX's PTFI stake to ~37% from 2042; IUPK extension application was submitted June 2026 and is not yet granted.
data_conflicts: Triage (Q13) cited ~$8.7bn operating cash flow on a $4,500 gold deck; the July 2026 release guides ~$8.3bn on a $4,000 gold deck (stale, not wrong when written).

Yahoo EV $121.9bn and EBITDA $9.55bn are consolidated including noncontrolling interests; FCX-attributable economics are smaller. Yahoo FCF $2.16bn differs from our OCF-less-capex TTM of $1.76bn (definition).
Yahoo TTM EPS 2.04 vs sum of four quarterly GAAP EPS 2.03 (rounding).
FCX.confidence_in_thesis: medium (operating facts verified in filings; the verdict rests on copper-price and ramp assumptions and the IUPK outcome is unresolved)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for FCX. Own reverse DCF: price implies ~31% annual owner-FCF growth from $2.5bn (fading to 3%) vs our base of ~13% a year over ten years (owner FCF $6.1bn by 2029), so the price implies more than base; only the bull case (~$73/share) reaches the price.

FCX.scenario_basis: Start $72.31; 2026E EPS ~3.05, FY27 Street 4.14. Base: 2029 EPS $5.30 (copper ~$6, Grasberg full rate) x 14x = $74 plus ~$1.8 dividends. Bear: copper ~$4.50, EPS $3.0 x 11x plus dividends. Bull: copper ~$7+, EPS $7.0 x 16x plus dividends.

CNC.thesis_one_line: Large US insurer for Medicaid, Obamacare and Medicare drug plans, repairing profits after a bad 2025, and priced as if the recovery stalls.
kill_criteria: FY2026 adjusted diluted EPS guidance floor (now "greater than $4.80", acc. 0001071739-26-000154) cut below $4.80 or withdrawn again (raised 3.00 to 3.40 to 4.80 in 2026).
Medicaid HBR above 94.5% in two consecutive quarters (Q1'26 93.1%, Q2'26 93.9%).
Consolidated debt-to-capital (total debt / (debt + equity), 10-Q liquidity section) above 47% (41.6% at 6/30/26).
First FY2027 adjusted EPS outlook (expected Feb 2027; none has been issued yet) below $5.00 (Street FY27 ~$5.35; FY26 floor $4.80).
NAIC aggregate risk-based capital below 300% of Authorized Control Level in the annual report (over 350% at 12/31/25).
key_adverse_facts: Guidance is a 'greater than' floor; 2025 guidance was withdrawn on 1 Jul 2025 (~$1.8bn lower risk-adjustment estimate, ~$2.75 EPS) and the 2025 GAAP forecast (loss not to exceed $12.85/share) was missed (actual -$13.53).
Medicaid HBR still 93.9% in Q2'26 (Q1 93.1%); Q4 is seasonally loss-making (Q4'25 adjusted -$1.19).
The 2026 guidance raise includes ~$0.50 of non-recurring items and H1 includes a $481m pre-tax benefit from final 2025 risk-adjustment results.
2027 policy risk: Medicaid work requirements and more frequent redeterminations (largely from 2027) and California moving ~250,000 UIS members out of managed care on 1 Jan 2027.

Securities class action (Lunstrum, filed 9 Jul 2025) plus five derivative suits; CFO retiring 31 Dec 2026; $10.8bn goodwill and $4.2bn intangibles (tangible equity ~$7.5bn); regulated subsidiaries hold $43.0bn of the $44.8bn cash and investments, only $1.8bn is unregulated/parent.
data_conflicts: V1 net debt of -$10.95bn (debt less consolidated cash) mixes regulated-subsidiary cash with parent debt; parent-level net debt is ~$14.3bn and EV ~$44.8bn, not $19.8bn, so V1's -25.9% implied growth is an artefact.
V1 base case (27% revenue CAGR, year-3 EPS $12.62, +67.7% a year) exceeds 2024 adjusted EPS of $7.17 and the Street 12-month high; not usable.

Yahoo/D3 TTM free cash flow (~$9bn) reflects float and payment timing; the b1 FCF-yield percentile of 0.99 is an artefact. Yahoo TTM revenue $180.3bn differs from D3/filings TTM $202.9bn (49,690+49,725+49,944+53,579); V1 flagged the 11.2% gap.
CNC.confidence_in_thesis: low-to-medium (recovery is visible in two quarters of filings and valuation is undemanding, but earnings depend on Medicaid rate adequacy and 2027 policy changes, and guidance is a floor)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: Direction agrees (cheap) but V1's inputs are wrong: net debt nets regulated-subsidiary cash against parent debt and the base case assumes 27% revenue growth and $12.62 year-3 EPS. Own reverse DCF at parent-level capital: price implies ~3-6% annual EPS growth vs our base ~8.6% ($5.0 to $6.4 by 2029, still below 2024's $7.17).

CNC.scenario_basis: Start $61.82; FY26E adjusted EPS ~$5.0 (guidance floor >$4.80; H1 actual $5.88); no dividend. Base: 2029 adjusted EPS $6.40 x 12x = $77. Bear: EPS $3.50 (Medicaid/Marketplace relapse) x 9x. Bull: EPS $8.50 x 14x.

EVRG.thesis_one_line: Kansas and Missouri electric utility adding data-centre customers and investing heavily; a solid, slow compounder whose price already credits the top of its growth target.
kill_criteria: FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance (now "$4.14 to $4.34", acc. 0001193125-26-336661) midpoint cut below $4.14 (the current low end), or reported FY2026 adjusted EPS below $4.14.
Consolidated debt / (debt + total equity) above 65% (61.6% at 6/30/26; debt $16.5bn, equity $10.3bn).
MPSC order in Evergy Metro's 2026 rate case (new rates expected Jan 2027) granting an authorised ROE below 9.5% (requested 10.5%).
No additional electric service agreement signed by 31 Dec 2026 (management: "at least one more"), or cancellation of any signed ESA.
Long-term adjusted EPS growth target (now "6% to 8%+", same accession) lowered below 6% a year, or 2027 guidance midpoint below $4.50 (Street FY27 $4.57).
key_adverse_facts: FY2025 adjusted EPS $3.83 missed the narrowed guidance range of $3.92-$4.02 (and the original $3.92-$4.12); cause cited: weather and demand headwinds.
Free cash flow about -$1.4bn TTM (H1'26 OCF $711m vs capex $1,812m); consolidated debt $16.5bn, debt/(debt+equity) 61.6%; new issues priced at 5.3-6.4%; H1 interest expense +11%.
Equity dilution: $1.2bn ATM programme (~$0.8bn left) with forward sales settling Mar 2027-Jul 2028; diluted shares 236.5m vs 230.9m basic.
Evergy Metro 2026 Missouri rate case (request ~$140m, 10.5% ROE) has a hearing in Oct 2026 with rates expected Jan 2027; outcome uncertain.
Short interest ~8.8% of float (Yahoo), elevated for a utility.
data_conflicts: Triage (Q14) did not mention the 2025 guidance miss.
Yahoo forward P/E 17.1x uses FY27 EPS ($4.57); on the 2026 guidance midpoint ($4.24) the multiple is 18.4x.
Yahoo trailing EPS 3.93 vs filings sum of GAAP quarters 3.94 (rounding).
EVRG.confidence_in_thesis: medium (regulated earnings are stable and 2026 is tracking, but the valuation conclusion flips with the discount rate: implied growth 5.6% to 8.1%)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for EVRG. Own reverse DCF (cost of equity 7.96%, 66% payout): price implies ~8.1% annual EPS growth for five years (5.6% at a 7.3% cost of equity) vs our base of 6.5%, so the price implies more than base on the project basis and is near fair only on the lower discount rate.

EVRG.scenario_basis: Start $78.04; 2026 adjusted EPS midpoint $4.24; dividend $2.78 growing ~4.5%/yr (~$8.9 over 3 years). Base: EPS +6.5%/yr to $5.12 x 17x = $87. Bear: EPS +3%/yr x 14.5x. Bull: EPS +8%/yr x 19x.
